newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London static, in light volume.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London static, in light volume.

text.p: U.S. shares were little changed in Europe late morning as many European participants pondered a possible Wall Street correction but remained unsure a near-term slide was inevitable.

"Nobody knows which way to jump at the moment," one market maker said. "We've seen a little bit of buying, a little selling but basically the market is trendless." "If the bond market remains weak the Dow will probably start a bit lower but after that it's anybodys' guess."
Dealers said a scarcity of corporate news over the weekend also contributed to the market uncertainty.
"The market needs some good corporate results or economic data to get it going again but sadly there isn't much on the horizon today," one dealer said.
High-technology shares were mostly firmer, led by IBM, which attracted some bargain hunting after last week's slide.
IBM was up $1/4 at $150-7/8, Intel rose $3/8 to $150-7/8, and Texas Instruments added $1/8 to $69-1/4.

Elsewhere, General Motors was down $1/4 at $62-1/4 while Ford dipped $1/8 to $33-1/2. With no U.S. economic data due on Monday, the market attention will turn to the U.S. Employment Cost Index, due on Tuesday, economists said.

"The Fed likes to watch the quarterly employment cost index closely. The monthly earnings data are more narrowly based, but provide good clues," said Robin Aspinall, strategist at National Australia Bank.
The fourth-quarter employment cost index is forecast to rise by 1.2 percent after a 0.6 percent increase the previous quarter, according to a Reuters poll of economists.
The March T-bond was down 6/32 at 110-2/32 while the March S&P 500 futures contract on Globex was up 1.25 at 771.00 by 1115 GMT.
